text:
Maria K: Quick heads-up — scheduling a rolling 'silent' reboot wave across AZ7 GPU nodes next Tue 03:00-05:00 UTC. This is to pick up the kernel hotfix and the NIC microcode that should reduce packet drops we saw last week. No customer-facing config changes planned; we expect a small tail latency bump for 60-120s per node as services restart.

Joel P: Can you share the node selector list + when each node will reboot? Need to update our deployment affinity to avoid thundering-herd.

Maria K: plan: reboot in 5 batches of ~40 nodes, 6-minute gap between reboots within a batch, 10m between batches. Reboot order is based on pool utilization and thermal profile. Script will do: cordon -> evict non-daemonsets -> reboot -> wait for kube-ready then uncordon.

Samir: For the eviction step use this command so we don't delete local caches:
```bash
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data=false --force
```
Also we will skip drains for Dedicated pools tagged 'no-evac' (customer SLA).

Alex T: How are we handling spot workloads? We need backfill policy to avoid capacity leaks and cost spikes.

Maria K: We'll run the spot backfill orchestrator to reschedule spot pods into AZ6 and AZ8 during the window. Backfill policy: limit each batch to 20% cross-zone movement. If we exceed 70% spot eviction rate, fall back to extra burst capacity (reserved spare = 100 GPUs) which we've provisioned.

Infra Bot: maintenance created: id=mt-az7-2026-03-24, window=2026-03-24T03:00Z-05:00Z, owner=maria.k

Lina: Network team — reminder: NIC microcode also requires a brief link flap on the host during update (~30s). We need egress-safety rules so customer connections don't drop across regional endpoints. Ops-oncall, any objections?

ops-oncall: noted. We'll provision temporary routing fallback to other regions for external traffic. Also will monitor p99 and open an incident if >15% request failures.

Joel P: Cost note — cross-zone backfill will create egress charges. Estimated additional cost: ~$2k for the window if we do full 5 batches. Should we enable smarter backfill to throttle based on cost alert?

Maria K: set backfill throttle to 60% if estimated egress > $1.5k. I'll add an override flag in the runbook.

Samir: Add a sanity check in the script:
```python
if estimated_egress_cost > threshold:
    scale_backfill(0.6)
```
and also emit events to ops channel.

Alex T: Will Dedicated customers see any impact?

Maria K: No planned impact. Nodes in Dedicated will be excluded unless explicitly patched by account. We will notify customers in advance with the standard banner.

Lina: I'll add a post-maint check: run connectivity probe and NIC counters diff. Script:
```bash
for node in ${PATCHED_NODES}; do
  ssh $node sudo ethtool -S eth0 | grep tx_ | wc -l
done
```
Infra Bot: reminder sent to #customer-notifications: "AZ7 maintenance: 2026-03-24 03:00-05:00 UTC — minimal impact expected."

ops-oncall: will be on-call with pages and will escalate at 03:15 if we see >2% error rate.

Maria K: thanks all. I'll post the runbook link tomorrow and schedule a dry-run this Friday 22:00 UTC.

Alex T: :thumbsup:
